text:
Ravi M: Following the postmortem, we need a single owner for vendor auth fallback work and a clear rollout plan. Recurring pattern: control-plane throttles -> token issuance fails -> model-registry write errors.
Jin T: I'll pick up the short-term mitigation: local token cache + adaptive backoff. POC in 48h, canary in 7 days.
Kai S: Long-term: dual auth providers + HSM/KMS key sync verification. I'll own that. Deliverables: design doc, compat shim, and migration plan. Target: design review in 12 days.
Nora V: We should centralize tracking. Suggest epic INF-7901 with subtasks and weekly status check-ins. I'll create it and add owner tags.
Ravi M: Yes. Make sure each subtask has an acceptance criteria e.g., "on 401 spike, flip to cached-mode within 30s" and test scenarios for regional control-plane degradation.
IncidentBot: Auto-note: attach incident timeline and perf graphs to INF-7901 when created.
Jin T: POC notes: using Redis cluster (small) for tokens keyed by service-account|scope. TTL 5m, jittered refresh, and metrics: token_cache_hit, token_refresh_latency, token_refresh_failures. Sample logic: 
```
if now > cached_token.expiry - 20s:
  refresh_async()
else:
  use(cached_token)
```
I'll add circuit breaker: >20% refresh_failures -> open for 2m.
Priya R: For writes to model-registry, we should queue writes during fallback and replay with idempotency keys. I can prototype a durable queue backed by S3 and lambda for retries. ETA 5 days for prototype.
Kai S: Dual-auth needs to preserve JWT claims shape for downstream. Plan: mapping layer that translates provider B tokens to expected claims. Back-compat grace period: 21 days.
Ravi M: Ops checklist: update runbook to include steps: mark impacted region, flip feature flag "auth:cached-mode", enable write-queue, and escalate to vendor. Also add the triage query for vendor-response-code + region in logs.
Nora V: Created INF-7901 and subtasks INF-7902 (token cache), INF-7903 (write-queue), INF-7904 (dual-auth design), INF-7905 (runbook + drills). Linking docs now.
DeployBot: Canary scheduled: roll token-cache to canary cluster on 2026-09-07T02:00Z. Will report status.
Jin T: Note on metrics: add alert for 5% 401s over 2m and a secondary alert for token_refresh_failures > 10/min. The alert should page infra and tag the incident channel.
Priya R: Replay logic for queued writes must be idempotent: include request fingerprint and last-applied timestamp. We'll include metrics for replay success and duplicate suppression.
Kai S: Also recommend vendor contract ask: dedicated auth endpoint SLA and control-plane rate limits per account. I'll draft negotiation points and propose a monthly resilience drill with vendor present.
Ravi M: Owners recap: Jin = token cache & alerts (48h POC), Priya = write-queue (5d prototype), Kai = dual-auth + SLA (12d design), Nora = epic + tracking + calendar invites. Ops to update runbook and add the escalation play.
Nora V: I'll create weekly status updates in the epic and set a recurring "Vendor Resilience" sync (monthly, 45m).
Jin T: POC done in 36h, uploading results to INF-7902. Found one edge-case: token refresh races for parallel workers. Adding a singleflight lock for refresh.
Ravi M: Good — post updates here daily until the canary is healthy. After canary, we'll run a simulated control-plane failure in canary and validate acceptance criteria.
Priya R: Will include a dry-run script to simulate 401s and the replay path.
IncidentBot: Reminder set: reconvene in 7 days for a status check.
Ravi M: Thanks everyone. If tasks slip, update INF-7901 and ping @Ravi M. :thumbsup:
